scenes.visualIntent: Problem-first hook extending no-arbitrage pricing to indices, FX, and physical commodities
keyElements: Most derivatives volume trades macro indices, FX, and commodities
Program trading algorithms replace impossible single-share orders
Covered Interest Parity and storage carry unify all global contracts

scenes.visualIntent: Explain how index arbitrage and automated program trading replicate constituent stock baskets
keyElements: Index futures compound spot at net carry rate (r - q)
Index arbitrage swaps futures against weighted constituent baskets
Program trading routes 500 stock orders within milliseconds

scenes.visualIntent: Contrast frictionless textbook myths with arbitrage bands and quarterly expiration surges
keyElements: Commissions and spreads carve a no-trade arbitrage band
Triple Witching quarterly unwinds spark sudden expiration volume
High-rate foreign currencies trade at forward discounts, not premiums

scenes.visualIntent: Derive Covered Interest Parity by modeling foreign interest rf as continuous dividend yield
keyElements: Foreign interest rate rf behaves exactly like dividend yield q
Covered Interest Parity sets F0 = S0 exp((r - rf) * T)
Premium or discount depends directly on domestic minus foreign rate

scenes.visualIntent: Trace the causal chain enforcing Covered Interest Parity across global money markets
keyElements: Parity breaks trigger instant riskless cross-currency trades
Forward FX hedge eliminates all currency exchange uncertainty
Borrowing, converting, investing, and hedging seal guaranteed spread

scenes.visualIntent: Solve textbook numerical example calculating 1-year USD/GBP forward rate at 1.4557
keyElements: Spot USD/GBP 1.5000 with US 5.0% and UK 8.0% creates -3.0% spread
Continuous carry factor exp(-0.03) gives forward discount 1.4557
Higher UK yield exactly offsets the cheaper forward pound conversion

scenes.visualIntent: Derive commodity carry adding storage u and subtracting physical convenience yield y
keyElements: Storage costs u lift investment metal futures like a negative dividend
Convenience yield y credits operational security of physical stock
Short-sale barriers leave consumption goods with only an upper bound

scenes.visualIntent: Synthesize all asset classes inside Hull's single Cost of Carry equation
keyElements: Every asset follows one master equation: F0 = S0 exp(cT)
Cost of carry c summarizes financing minus yield plus storage
Global trading desks map all markets onto this unified parameter c

scenes.visualIntent: Contrast upward contango carry forces against downward backwardation and short delivery options
keyElements: Contango curves trade above spot when interest and storage dominate
Normal backwardation discounts futures when hedgers pay risk premiums
Delivery options let shorts choose timing, warehouse, and cheapest grade

scenes.visualIntent: 3-beat interactive quiz solving 1-year EUR/USD forward premium 1.2753
keyElements: Spot 1.2500 with US 6.0% and Eurozone 4.0% yields +2.0% carry
Positive domestic spread lifts forward quote to 1.2753 USD/EUR
Lower foreign interest earns a compensating forward currency premium

scenes.visualIntent: Synthesize Chapter 5 macro forward pricing and bridge clearly to Chapter 6 Interest Rate Futures
keyElements: Unified Cost of Carry F0 = S0 exp(cT) governs all asset classes
Friction bands and short delivery options create real-world spreads
Chapter 6 next covers Interest Rate Futures, day counts, and Treasury bonds

scenes.visualIntent: Fixed 6-beat summary thread consolidating all 8 macro forward pricing principles from Part 2
keyElements: Program trading keeps index futures within transaction bands
Covered Interest Parity maps foreign rate differentials to FX forwards
